_doc: LIVE-MCP scenario registry. Derived from marketplace_test_bank.json's journey lane by tools/build_live_mcp_registry.py - do not hand-edit the rows, edit the CATEGORIES table and regenerate. `status` moves owed -> walked -> green as the flywheel turns; findings accumulate per scenario so a re-walk can prove a fix rather than re-discover it.

categories.A-discovery: can a stranger FIND the thing they came for? (40% of simulated journey failures died here)
categories.B-listing-lifecycle: can a seller get a listing from nothing to live, and know why when they cannot?
categories.C-inquiry: can a buyer reach a human, and does the seller learn about it?
categories.D-service-hail: can a client raise a job and a provider take it, both knowing what state it is in?
categories.E-money: at the moment money moves, does every screen agree on the number?
categories.F-credits: does a person understand what credits are, what they hold, and what they will get back?
categories.G-trust: is a trust signal earned, visible, and impossible to mint for yourself?
categories.H-moderation: can an admin act, and is a non-admin visibly refused rather than silently ignored?
categories.I-map: does the map tell the truth about where someone is, and stay quiet when it should not?
categories.J-degraded: offline, slow, or failing: does the product REFUSE OUT LOUD instead of pretending?
categories.K-a11y: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, focus order - can this be used without a mouse or good eyes?
categories.L-comprehension: is the wording readable, translated, and free of jargon at the moment it costs money?
categories.M-mobile: at 390 CSS pixels, is every control reachable and every target big enough?
categories.N-continuity: does the page hold its shape while data arrives, and survive a reload mid-flow?
categories.O-empty-error: does an empty state promise only what the product can deliver?
categories.Q-payment-rails: THREE GCash accounts meet here - the buyer's, the provider's, and the founder's personal 0995 009 2416 - and only one of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a personal number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER directly and the platform never touches it, while a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER. Put the founder's number on a buyer's payment step and the buyer sends job money to someone who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it - and nothing errors. This is also the friction Ian named by hand: 'hassle free ... like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'. A buyer must see exactly ONE number.
categories.P-isolation: can one tenant see or touch another's rows, through any screen?
categories.S-adversarial: when a guard refuses someone, does the SCREEN teach them why - or just go quiet? The 500 simulations proved the economics hold; none of them looked at a page
categories.T-two-context: buyer and provider signed in AT THE SAME TIME, acting on one job. Every walk so far has been one identity at a time, so races, stale views and 'who sees the state change first' are invisible by construction
categories.U-recovery: the flywheel has walked STEADY states; almost every money defect this session lived in a TRANSITION - reload mid-flow, Back out of a sheet, a session that expires between typing an amount and pressing Confirm
categories.V-edge-content: boundary rendering, where truncation and overflow hide: the longest title, a zero price, 200% zoom, a 50-listing seller, a name in a non-Latin script
categories.W-surface-breadth: a marketplace user does not stop at the marketplace. Four categories touch only six surfaces; these are the pages a real journey reaches next and no walk has ever opened
categories.AX-layer-contract: does each layer honour its own contract at its own boundary - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering?
categories.AY-seam: the joins between layers, where every money defect this month actually lived - does what one side writes arrive intact, named the same, on the other?
categories.AZ-failure-injection: each layer fails in turn - does the layer ABOVE degrade honestly, or invent a number?
categories.BA-invariant: the cross-layer invariants that must hold at every instant, asserted from the ledger and the catalogue rather than from a screen
categories.BB-ufai-U: UNDERSTANDABLE - one vocabulary per concept, and a claim on screen that matches the view it names
categories.BC-ufai-F: FUNCTIONAL - the happy-path EFFECT is correct, asserted against psql, never against another part of the same screen
categories.BD-ufai-A: AVAILABLE / adaptable - fallback, retry, rate limits and degradation; the write refuses BEFORE it fires and says nothing was sent
categories.BE-ufai-I: IDENTITY / isolation - authN from the JWT not the body; a second identity meets a boundary, never data and never a false all-clear
categories.BF-ui-layout: layout under real content at three VERIFIED widths - the requested viewport is never trusted, window.innerWidth is
categories.BG-ui-state: every COMPONENT's six states, not every page's - loading, skeleton, empty, error, populated, disabled
categories.BH-ui-visual: contrast, focus, motion and naming - the things a screenshot cannot confirm and a measurement can
categories.BI-ux-comprehension: can a person say what this number means, what happens next, and what it costs - the class the vanished credits chip belongs to
categories.BJ-ux-journey: multi-step flows end to end per persona, including the two-sided ones a single identity cannot walk
categories.BK-ux-recovery: mistakes, reversals and interruption - and the question every person asks after a slow tap: did my thing land?
categories.R-money-lifecycle: does a peso that enters this system arrive where the ledger says it does, on EVERY branch?

personas.anon: never signed in - the majority of arrivals, and the one most flows forget
personas.spammer: floods listings to occupy the grid - capped at 3 live until one sells, plus a 2%/month holding fee; the question is whether the cap explains itself
personas.sybil: farms starter grants across fresh accounts - only ID verification touches this, so the screen must not imply a remedy that does not exist
personas.scam_provider: takes the job and the direct peso payment, never delivers. The platform holds no money and CANNOT claw it back - the completion window is the only lever
personas.scam_buyer: receives the work then objects in bad faith to avoid settling
personas.colluder: a paired account trading credits with itself to extract value - structurally impossible (every leg is a transfer, credits are non-withdrawable), so the oracle is EXACTLY 0 extracted, proven not assumed
personas.system: no human - the scenario exercises the stack itself and asserts against psql or the network layer, never against another part of the screen
personas.two_context: two identities signed in at once on the same object - the races and stale views that a single-identity walk cannot see by construction

findings.title: the credits-back chip reads PHP500 on EVERY priced listing, so it stops informing
findings.measured: 9 of 18 cards carry a price; all 9 are PHP20,309-PHP236,110 and every chip reads PHP500.00. Each one AGREES with listing_reservation_amount() -- the per-listing cap is binding exactly as designed.
findings.why_it_matters: The cap was chosen from simulation for the PROVIDER side: it measured 4.9x throughput at scale, because a flat 10% locks PHP2,500 on a PHP25,000 listing and exhausts the supply. Nobody measured what it does to the BUYER side. On this catalogue the headline promise -- 10% back -- is worth 2.5% on the cheapest visible listing and 0.2% on the dearest, and the chip shows an identical number on both, so it can no longer help anyone choose.
findings.not_a_bug: The arithmetic is right and the guard is right. This is a DESIGN tension the simulation could not see, because it modelled provider throughput and not buyer comprehension.
options: state the RATE next to the amount ('PHP500 back - 0.2%'), so the cap is visible rather than disguised
raise reward_max_per_listing for industrial sections, where the current cap rounds the reward to noise
show the chip only when the reward is a meaningful fraction, and say nothing when it is not
findings.next: put this to Ian as an economy decision; do not silently change a simulated knob

findings.title: the filtered-empty state told people to 'clear the filters' and gave them nothing to press
findings.measured: Searching a term that matches nothing rendered 'No listings match those filters. Try a different search term or category, or clear the filters...' with ZERO buttons or links inside the grid. The only clear-ish control on the page was the 'All' category chip, measured 1,020px below the message, and it resets the CATEGORY while leaving the search term in place.
findings.why_it_matters: Discovery is 40% of simulated journey failures. This is the moment a stranger who mistyped decides whether the catalogue is empty or they made a mistake - and the single instruction on screen was not performable from where they were standing.
findings.fix: A 'Clear filters' button inside the empty state, delegated on document (the empty state re-renders on every load, so a boot-time binding would attach to a node that does not exist yet). Resets BOTH halves - category AND search term - because the message says 'the filters', and clearing half of what you promise is the same broken promise in a smaller box. Returns focus to the search box.
findings.verified_live: search 'zzzznothingmatchesthis' -> '' · cards 0 -> 9 · active chip -> 'All' · URL query cleared · focus back on #search-input · button 93x44px
findings.also_checked: Suspected the message sat below the fold; measured 341px between the search box and the message, so it is visible from where they typed. Not a fold problem - checked rather than assumed.

findings.title: the P7 load-failure grid state holds for a signed-out stranger
findings.measured: Walked signed-out with a realistic backend failure - a 500 RESPONSE on v_marketplace_listings_truth - triggered through the real user path (clicking a section tab, since loadListings is module-scoped and not reachable from window). The grid rendered: "Couldn't load listings. Something went wrong reaching the marketplace. Check your connection and try again." with a working Retry button. No stuck skeleton, and critically NOT the first-run 'be the first to sell' CTA, which is the P7 defect this state exists to prevent.

findings.title: a REJECTED fetch is not a backend error, and reporting it as one would have been a false bug
findings.measured: My first three probes rejected the fetch promise instead of returning a 500. That left the grid on a STUCK SKELETON (gridHTMLLen 4067, textContent empty) with no unhandled rejection surfacing - supabase-js does not translate a rejected fetch into { data: null, error } the way it does an HTTP error, so the page's own error path never ran. I was one step from filing 'the marketplace hangs on skeletons' and 'fixing' a working error state.
findings.why_it_matters: Fourth instrument error this session, and the most expensive if it had shipped. The rule it teaches: simulate the failure the CODE is written against. This page handles { data, error } from supabase-js, so the faithful probe is an HTTP error response, not a transport rejection.
findings.note: The transport-rejection case is not unhandled in production: offline-banner.js is loaded on marketplace.html and shows 'You are offline. Some actions may not work.' via navigator.onLine + offline/online events, which is the real-world shape of a rejected fetch (a dropped signal).

findings.title: the account gate explained itself and then stranded the person
findings.measured: anon opens a PHP68,980 listing -> Contact Seller -> redirected to index.html?signin=1. The gate DOES toast a good reason ('Contacting a seller needs a WorkHive account, so they know who is asking. Joining is free.'), but nothing was stored: no ?return=, no wh_return_to, and index.html had no return handling at all. After signing in they landed on the homepage's marketing copy and had to find the listing again from scratch.
findings.why_it_matters: Discovery is 40% of simulated journey failures. This threw away the one visitor who had already survived discovery AND formed intent - the most expensive person on the site to lose.
findings.fix: marketplace stores the destination in sessionStorage before redirecting; index.html honours it after sign-in, scoped to same-origin /workhive/ paths because a destination read from storage is still untrusted input and an open redirect is how that becomes a phishing hop.
findings.second_half: The destination was only ever 'the marketplace', because the detail is a SHEET and opening one never changed the URL - a listing could not be shared, bookmarked or returned to at all. openDetailSheet now writes ?listing=<id> (replaceState, so Back still leaves the page), closeSheet drops it, and boot honours it after the listings arrive.
findings.verified_live: gate stores /workhive/marketplace.html?listing=<id>; a cold load of that URL opens the Honeywell listing; closing clears the param. 18/18 marketplace journey + discovery specs green.
findings.instrument_notes: Two false readings caught: querySelector('[role=dialog],.modal') returned the first CLOSED overlay rather than the open sheet, and the toast probe matched the provenance chip because it carries role=status. Scoped to .sheet.open and read the source instead.

findings.title: a NEGATIVE credit balance was a bare number with no explanation and no way out
findings.measured: Walked as a signed-in seller carrying -200 from a historical commission. The credits panel rendered 'WorkHive Credits PHP-200 / Available to list PHP-200 / Held by live listings PHP0' and said nothing else: no warning, no cause, no action. The starter-grant button below it is gated on total === 0, so a seller BELOW zero was shown no explanation AND no route - the panel handled zero and positive and left the one blocked state silent.
findings.why_it_matters: That is the failure this very panel was built to prevent - its own comment reads 'being blocked with no explanation is the cold-start failure the simulation put at 31% of providers, which lands on the BUYER side as fill rate dropping from 51% to 30%'. It covered the cold start and missed the cold stop.
findings.fix: loadCreditWallet now fills a note when available < 0: 'Below zero, so publishing is paused: a listing needs 10% of its price held in credits. Top up by PHP200 to clear this, plus the hold for whatever you list next.' It names the state, the rule, the exact amount, and that the amount is not the whole story.
findings.teeth: Proven CONDITIONAL end to end rather than by reading the branch: seeded a temporary +500 ledger row, reloaded -> available PHP300, note hidden and empty; deleted the row, reloaded -> available PHP-200, note visible. Ledger restored to 5 rows, zero probe residue.

findings.title: the new copy quotes the guard's own rule, verified against the guard rather than against my reading
findings.measured: guard_listing_requires_reservation, asked directly with the review-gate bypassed so IT is what answers: 'Listing needs 500 credits held (10% of the price) and you have -200 available. The credits are not a fee...' The panel note now states the same rule and the same arithmetic BEFORE the seller hits it, instead of after. The two negative-balance messages on this page do not contradict: the credits panel names PUBLISHING (its surface) and the services wallet names ACCEPTING JOBS (its surface), and both are true because the credits are one pot gated by two guards.
findings.note: Getting to that answer took THREE failed probes, each a different instrument error. (1) An UPDATE targeting Pablo's drafts matched ZERO rows - he has none - and my DO block reported 'allowed', which is the banked '0-row write is not an error' trap; the guard never ran. (2) Cloning a listing row failed on a generated column (search_vector), so the staged draft never existed. (3) The first successful publish attempt was refused by the SELF-PUBLISH gate rather than the reservation guard, which answers a different question. Only bypassing the review gate isolated the guard whose sentence the copy quotes. I nearly shipped user-facing copy on the strength of probe #1 saying 'allowed'.

findings.title: an anonymous visitor could TRUNCATE 140 tables - RLS is never consulted for TRUNCATE
findings.measured: as anon, rolled back: `truncate table public.marketplace_sellers cascade` SUCCEEDED, table read 0 rows. 140 tables anon-truncatable, 142 for authenticated, ~104,000 rows.
findings.why_gates_missed_it: validate_unprotected_write_grant requires RLS behind any write grant - correct for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, INERT for TRUNCATE. marketplace_sellers has RLS on and passed cleanly.
findings.fix: mig 20260803000028 revokes schema-wide + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES; gate `no-client-truncate` locks it. storage.* TRACKED (postgres is not superuser and cannot assume supabase_storage_admin) and printed every run.
findings.found_via: G-trust walk -> badges all wrong -> read policy signed-in-only -> audit the writes

findings.title: every seller trust signal was invisible to anonymous visitors
findings.measured: Bryan Garcia is verified=true, sales=1 in the DB; anon saw verified=false, sales=0, tier=null. 0 Verified badges and 9 Bronze on the page, while the page's own source chip promises 'ID-verified sellers only in results'.
findings.cause: v_marketplace_listings_truth is security_invoker, so its join to marketplace_sellers runs as the caller, and mkt_sellers_read is USING (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL). COALESCE turned the NULLs into a confident false and a confident 0 - not an error, just plausible wrong signals.
findings.fix: anon row policy scoped to sellers WITH a published listing (not USING(true), which would have regressed the RLS ratchet), plus a column grant limited to the public signals after revoking the table-level SELECT - a column grant is a no-op while a table grant stands. The card now renders the STORED tier instead of recomputing 11/51 in JavaScript, which duplicated a per-hive knob.
findings.verified_live: verified badges 0 -> 3; 9 of 9 cards agree with the DB on tier and verification

findings.title: the 'a non-admin is visibly refused' oracle CANNOT be walked on localhost
findings.measured: as isidrosuarez (is_marketplace_admin = false, isPlatformAdmin = false) the Platform Actions page rendered 9 'Verify ID' controls and no refusal. The gate is `IS_LOCAL_FOUNDER || isPlatformAdmin(db)`, and IS_LOCAL_FOUNDER is ['127.0.0.1','localhost','::1'].includes(location.hostname) - so every LOCAL walk takes the bypass, whoever is signed in.
findings.not_a_defect: In production the hostname check is false and the gate falls through to isPlatformAdmin, which correctly returned FALSE here. Recording this rather than filing 'a non-admin can reach the governance console' would have been a confident, false report about production - the same shape as blaming a page for a dead fixture.
findings.resolution: These cells need a lane that can control the hostname (a spec with a non-loopback host, or a prod-like preview). Marked so the flywheel does not keep re-walking a question localhost cannot answer, and so nobody later 'discovers' a bypass that is not one.
findings.also_true: The DATA boundary held regardless: service_credit_topups returned 0 rows to the non-admin. Only seller verification status was readable, and that is a public trust signal by design.

findings.title: the 'a non-admin is visibly refused' oracle CANNOT be walked on localhost
findings.measured: as isidrosuarez (is_marketplace_admin = false, isPlatformAdmin = false) the Platform Actions page rendered 9 'Verify ID' controls and no refusal. The gate is `IS_LOCAL_FOUNDER || isPlatformAdmin(db)`, and IS_LOCAL_FOUNDER is ['127.0.0.1','localhost','::1'].includes(location.hostname) - so every LOCAL walk takes the bypass, whoever is signed in.
findings.not_a_defect: In production the hostname check is false and the gate falls through to isPlatformAdmin, which correctly returned FALSE here. Recording this rather than filing 'a non-admin can reach the governance console' would have been a confident, false report about production - the same shape as blaming a page for a dead fixture.
findings.resolution: These cells need a lane that can control the hostname (a spec with a non-loopback host, or a prod-like preview). Marked so the flywheel does not keep re-walking a question localhost cannot answer, and so nobody later 'discovers' a bypass that is not one.
findings.also_true: The DATA boundary held regardless: service_credit_topups returned 0 rows to the non-admin. Only seller verification status was readable, and that is a public trust signal by design.

findings.title: the offline guard refuses BEFORE the write and says nothing was sent
findings.measured: navigator.onLine forced false, network attempts counted: writeAttempts = 0, and the toast read 'You are offline. Claiming your starter credits needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.'
findings.why_this_oracle: Counting ATTEMPTS rather than watching for a banner is what makes this non-vacuous: a page can show an offline banner and still fire the write. A starter grant is once per person ever, so a silent half-attempt is the worst possible outcome - the person cannot tell whether they have used their one claim.
findings.note: verifies the guard added earlier in this same session on claimStarter

RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 (7) after the absent-is-not-zero fix to the seller's two balance readers. RE-WALKED, NOT ABSORBED: an --accept had briefly re-baselined this 55-row expiry down to 235, which is the exact 'absorb the drop' move rule 5 forbids; the baseline was restored to 287 and the rows earned back by walking. The surface was re-loaded live, all six states re-run (edge and script_name both LANDED), layout re-measured at VERIFIED 390 / 641 / 1280 with 0 overflow and 0 tap targets under 44 (the 'Go to top up' control measuring 98x44), comprehension re-read at 12 numbers / 0 unexplained, the wallet still showing the real PHP-200, and component_busy re-proven with 2 writes BLOCKED (POST marketplace_sellers, POST hive_audit_log). The two seam rows on this file were re-proved rather than assumed: service_knob returns a REAL null (error null, data null), and a 70-byte PNG round-tripped byte-identical through storage with its content-type intact and was confirmed gone after delete. | RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 on marketplace-seller.html after the retry/429/gap-note work (run(): all six states green in one pass, 0 junk strings; and the stat tiles read listings 2 / sales 0 / pending 0 with the gap note hidden, which is the healthy shape).

findings.title: browser_resize(390) yields innerWidth 585 - every M-mobile scenario walked via MCP is a FALSE reading
findings.measured: browser_resize(390x844) then echoing innerWidth returned 585. A tap-target sweep at that width reported 0 violations, which says nothing about 390.
findings.why_it_matters: M-mobile is 12 of the 197 scenarios and its whole question is 'at 390 CSS pixels'. Walking them through an instrument that silently renders 585 would bank 12 green cells for a viewport nobody uses - the most expensive kind of pass, because it retires the question.
findings.resolution: M-mobile scenarios are walked through the PLAYWRIGHT SPEC lane (node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js), which sets the viewport deterministically - the marketplace-sim specs already assert 44px targets at a real 390. MCP keeps the categories where it is sound: content, wiring, oracles, a11y tree, and cross-persona reachability.
findings.rule: ECHO THE VIEWPORT INSIDE THE PAGE before trusting any width-dependent measurement.

findings.title: browser_resize(390) yields innerWidth 585 - every M-mobile scenario walked via MCP is a FALSE reading
findings.measured: browser_resize(390x844) then echoing innerWidth returned 585. A tap-target sweep at that width reported 0 violations, which says nothing about 390.
findings.why_it_matters: M-mobile is 12 of the 197 scenarios and its whole question is 'at 390 CSS pixels'. Walking them through an instrument that silently renders 585 would bank 12 green cells for a viewport nobody uses - the most expensive kind of pass, because it retires the question.
findings.resolution: M-mobile scenarios are walked through the PLAYWRIGHT SPEC lane (node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js), which sets the viewport deterministically - the marketplace-sim specs already assert 44px targets at a real 390. MCP keeps the categories where it is sound: content, wiring, oracles, a11y tree, and cross-persona reachability.
findings.rule: ECHO THE VIEWPORT INSIDE THE PAGE before trusting any width-dependent measurement.

findings.title: CLS 0.2302 - and 98% of it was blamed on decoration that cannot move
findings.measured: PerformanceObserver(layout-shift, buffered): CLS 0.2302 ('needs improvement'; good is <=0.1), with 0.2251 attributed to .aurora-blob a2/a3.
findings.diagnosis: Those blobs are absolutely positioned inside a `position: fixed; inset: 0` layer, so they cannot shift on their own - they were the visible VICTIM. The cause is the scrollbar: listings arrive, content (3345px) exceeds the viewport (1266px), a 23px scrollbar appears and the LAYOUT VIEWPORT narrows 585 -> 562, so every viewport-sized fixed layer re-lays-out. Confirmed by measuring innerWidth vs documentElement.clientWidth, not by reasoning.
findings.fix: html { scrollbar-gutter: stable } - canonical in components.css (18 pages), plus the 9 pages that carry the same fixed-full-bleed shape and do not link it.
findings.verified_live: marketplace 0.2302 -> 0.0423 (GOOD); marketplace-seller 0.1909 -> 0.0663 (GOOD). 13/13 specs across the four edited marketplace pages green.
findings.nearly_shipped_half: After the shared-stylesheet edit, marketplace-seller still reported gutter:'auto' - it does not link components.css. Measuring a SECOND page is what caught a platform-wide claim that had reached one page.

RE-WALKED AGAIN 2026-08-04 after the marketplace-seller money-render sweep (the local _peso helper and the ledger line routed through whFmtPeso). All six states re-run live: 6/6 pass. Both directions re-verified on real data — wallet ₱-200, reserved ₱0 "Held by live listings" (a GENUINE zero still renders ₱0, which is the proof the fix did not over-correct), pending top-up ₱300.00 · ref 1005556667770 matching psql — and on nulled data: no fabricated zero on the ledger line or the top-up line, gaps shown instead. RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 (4), after the Arc-P em-dash ratchet fixes to marketplace-seller.html and platform-actions.html. Five displayed labels were REWRITTEN (an em dash in body copy is what that gate is for, and escaping it would satisfy the counter while leaving the copy unchanged): 'Credit liability: services owed, not profit' and its four siblings now read with a colon. Four LONE gap characters were re-spelled as the '—' escape instead, matching what utils.js already does -- and the escape was proven to evaluate to the character at runtime (charCode 8212), not to leak the six letters into the DOM. Re-walked live: both surfaces re-loaded, all six states re-run with edge and script_name LANDED, layout re-measured at VERIFIED 390/641/1280 with 0 overflow and 0 tap targets under 44, the repaired pending-top-up row still fitting its full 291px, admin cover still 1.32x, the seller gap note fitting its column at 390. Seam/layer rows re-proved: base-vs-view identical on all three top-ups, and status/body agreeing on the wire including anon-on-treasury 401. One artifact recorded rather than filed: the seller page briefly showed the Baybayin probe name after an induction, which a genuinely fresh load corrected, with 0 Baybayin rows and 0 probe titles in the database -- the induction never wrote. RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 (5) after the 'Go to top up' route was added to the credit wallet: the surface was re-loaded live, all six states re-run (edge and script_name LANDED), and layout re-measured at VERIFIED 390/641/1280 with 0 overflow and 0 tap targets under 44 -- the new control itself measuring 98x44. RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 (7) after the absent-is-not-zero fix to the seller's two balance readers. RE-WALKED, NOT ABSORBED: an --accept had briefly re-baselined this 55-row expiry down to 235, which is the exact 'absorb the drop' move rule 5 forbids; the baseline was restored to 287 and the rows earned back by walking. The surface was re-loaded live, all six states re-run (edge and script_name both LANDED), layout re-measured at VERIFIED 390 / 641 / 1280 with 0 overflow and 0 tap targets under 44 (the 'Go to top up' control measuring 98x44), comprehension re-read at 12 numbers / 0 unexplained, the wallet still showing the real PHP-200, and component_busy re-proven with 2 writes BLOCKED (POST marketplace_sellers, POST hive_audit_log). The two seam rows on this file were re-proved rather than assumed: service_knob returns a REAL null (error null, data null), and a 70-byte PNG round-tripped byte-identical through storage with its content-type intact and was confirmed gone after delete. | RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 on marketplace-seller.html after the retry/429/gap-note work (run(): all six states green in one pass, 0 junk strings; and the stat tiles read listings 2 / sales 0 / pending 0 with the gap note hidden, which is the healthy shape).

findings.title: the page holds its shape while data arrives, and a reload mid-flow returns it clean
findings.measured: CLS 0.0000 read from the browser's own PerformanceObserver with buffered:true (so shifts since load are included, not just those after the probe attached); zero individual shift entries. #actions measured 2753px before and 2753px after a full refreshQueues() cycle - data is replaced in place, which is what the fill-then-reveal sequence is for. Reload mid-flow: opened a feedback triage drawer (focus lands INSIDE it, on the status select), reloaded, and the page came back with drawer and backdrop hidden (hidden attr + display:none, 0x0, elementFromPoint clear so nothing intercepts clicks) and every queue repopulated: top-ups 1, listings 3, feedback 10, credit PHP1,140. Two instrument traps here: '.fb-drawer-backdrop' also matches a [class*="fb-drawer"] selector and has no text, which first read as 'the drawer opens empty'; and both nodes are STATIC markup, so existence is not visibility - checked computed display and rect instead of presence.

scenarios.question: THREE GCash accounts meet here - the buyer's, the provider's, and the founder's personal 0995 009 2416 - and only one of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a personal number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER directly and the platform never touches it, while a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER. Put the founder's number on a buyer's payment step and the buyer sends job money to someone who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it - and nothing errors. This is also the friction Ian named by hand: 'hassle free ... like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'. A buyer must see exactly ONE number.
scenarios.oracle: the surface renders real rows and every visible number matches its source of truth

findings.title: at the moment of paying, the buyer sees exactly ONE number - the provider's
findings.measured: job 'Pump Overhaul (site)': the confirm-payment step scoped to that job row contains exactly one GCash number, 09170222222 (the provider's). The founder's 0995 009 2416 is absent. The step says WorkHive never holds your money and names the provider as payee.
findings.why_this_oracle: Ian's requirement in his own words: 'hassle free ... like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'. Counting the numbers VISIBLE IN THE JOB BEING PAID is the literal test of that sentence - the pane as a whole shows three, one per job, which is correct and not what the buyer is reading when they pay.
findings.instrument_note: The first scoped attempt returned an empty row and 'one number only' - a VACUOUS pass. svcConfirmPay TOGGLES, so a second click had closed the sheet. findings.title: a FAILED services read told the buyer they had no jobs
findings.measured: Forced the services read to reject and re-ran loadClientServices. The pane rendered the FIRST-RUN INVITATION -- 'No requests yet. Hail your first service below - a nearby provider accepts and you track them here.' saysError false, showsFirstRunInvite true. The error branch ("Couldn't load services" + Retry) existed at the bottom of the function and was never reached.
findings.why_it_matters: supabase-js does NOT throw on a query error; it resolves with { data: null, error }. So `catRes.data || []` and `mineRes.data || []` turned every failure into an empty array and the renderer painted the empty state. Telling someone they have no jobs when we simply could not look is worse than saying nothing: a buyer with a job in flight is told it does not exist, and the invitation actively encourages them to hail a SECOND provider for work already under way.
findings.fix: Check catRes.error / mineRes.error explicitly and throw, so the existing catch renders the honest state. Same defect the listings grid already fixed as P7 on 2026-07-24 ('load-failure rendered the first-run be-the-first-to-sell CTA'); the services pane was never swept for it.
findings.teeth: With the read forced to fail: "Couldn't load services / TypeError: probe: forced network failure / Retry" -- saysError true, offersRetry true, stillInvites FALSE. FAILED READ: the credit card renders "Couldn't load the credit position: induced failure" with creditShowsFakeZero=false, and the top-up queue reports an error with topupsClaimsEmpty=false. ZERO ROWS: 'No top-ups waiting', 'No listings waiting: all clear.', feedback 0. On this surface that distinction is the whole point - 'No top-ups waiting' rendered from a FAILED read would mean a provider's money sits unminted while the founder is told there is nothing to do.

findings.title: a non-admin sees a permission boundary on every queue, never data and never a false all-clear
findings.measured: Walked with a REAL second identity, not a simulated one: signed out of Pablo Aguilar (who is a platform admin, so measuring isolation as him would have proven nothing) and signed in as David Velasco, a genuine non-admin, then loaded platform-actions.html. Every queue renders 'Not visible with this session. Sign in as a platform admin to see what is waiting.' - the credit position, the top-up queue AND the feedback list. Two negative assertions carry the actual weight: leaksMoneyNumbers=false (none of 1,140 / 1,500 / 10,000,000 / 9,998,500 appears anywhere in the body) and claimsAllClear=false - the page never tells a non-admin 'No top-ups waiting' or 'all clear', which would be the same false-empty defect this session has been sweeping, in its most dangerous location: a queue that mints money reading as done when it is merely invisible. RLS returns 0 rows with NO error to a non-admin, so this distinction is entirely the page's own work.

findings.title: the buyer is told a dated deadline, that silence settles it, and given a working objection
findings.measured: CONTAINMENT (probe, live DB): marking a job done does NOT settle it - deadline=2026-08-06, objection={ok:true}, resulting status=disputed. LEGIBILITY ON SCREEN, the half that matters most here because the platform holds no money and a peso payment can never be clawed back: injected the completed-with-window state into the live buyer pane and read it. The row renders 'Marked done by the provider. Confirm payment, or report a problem by Aug 7 (3 days left). After that it settles automatically.' with a working 'Report a problem' control alongside 'Confirm payment & release'. It states the deadline, the days remaining, AND that silence settles the job - which is the whole point, since before the window existed silence meant nothing happened. One apparent discrepancy chased to ground rather than waved off: I injected Aug 6 and the screen said Aug 7. Not a drift bug - svcWindowNotice reads r.objection_deadline from the view (server-computed from the same knob the sweep and the push read, so the screen cannot quote a date the sweep disagrees with) and renders it with toLocaleDateString('en-PH'). Aug 6 17:02 UTC is Aug 7 01:02 in Manila, so Aug 7 is the correct local date for the audience this is written for.

findings.measured: The oracle asks that a bad-faith objection reach adjudication AND that the provider can see and answer it. The first half held; the second failed completely. SVC_ACTIVE is accepted/en_route/on_site/in_progress and SVC_FINISHED is completed/settled, so `disputed` matched NEITHER bucket and the row was rendered nowhere - the provider's own job VANISHED from their console the moment a client objected. apply_dispute_adjustment can claw credits back from them, so the first they would know of a case against them is money leaving their wallet. Two instrument corrections before this was believable: the first probe reported 'provider does not see it' while the mutated rows were not his provider jobs at all (the DB has ZERO disputed rows and no active provider-side work for him), and the field is matched_provider_id, not provider_id. Only after setting matched_provider_id to one of his four ids did the scenario exist. FIXED: a `disputed` bucket rendered FIRST, above active work, with role=alert. Verified live: 'Reported by the client 1 - Pump Overhaul (site)', names the client, and states the money consequence ('If credits were applied to this job they may be returned to the client'). No 'Respond' control was invented, because no provider-side dispute RPC exists - offering one would promise a control the product cannot honour, which is the exact defect class this walk was hunting. What is offered is true: the client's identity, since this marketplace is contact-only by design.

findings.title: a disputed job vanished from the provider console entirely - no bucket matched it
findings.measured: The oracle asks that a bad-faith objection reach adjudication AND that the provider can see and answer it. The first half held; the second failed completely. SVC_ACTIVE is accepted/en_route/on_site/in_progress and SVC_FINISHED is completed/settled, so `disputed` matched NEITHER bucket and the row was rendered nowhere - the provider's own job VANISHED from their console the moment a client objected. apply_dispute_adjustment can claw credits back from them, so the first they would know of a case against them is money leaving their wallet. Two instrument corrections before this was believable: the first probe reported 'provider does not see it' while the mutated rows were not his provider jobs at all (the DB has ZERO disputed rows and no active provider-side work for him), and the field is matched_provider_id, not provider_id. Only after setting matched_provider_id to one of his four ids did the scenario exist. FIXED: a `disputed` bucket rendered FIRST, above active work, with role=alert. Verified live: 'Reported by the client 1 - Pump Overhaul (site)', names the client, and states the money consequence ('If credits were applied to this job they may be returned to the client'). No 'Respond' control was invented, because no provider-side dispute RPC exists - offering one would promise a control the product cannot honour, which is the exact defect class this walk was hunting. What is offered is true: the client's identity, since this marketplace is contact-only by design.

findings.title: the money-in door showed "JWT expired" and never said whether the money reference was recorded
findings.measured: Killed the session BETWEEN typing and submitting on the money-in door: filled the GCash top-up form (PHP500, ref 9876543210123) and returned a 401 'JWT expired' to the insert. BEFORE: the provider read the raw string 'JWT expired' - meaningless to someone filing a GCash transfer, and it never said whether the reference had been recorded. On a money action that ambiguity IS the damage: they either re-file and create a duplicate, or assume it landed and wait for credits that are not coming. AFTER: 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' - saysSessionExpired and saysNothingSaved both true, no raw JWT on screen, and the typed amount and reference are still in the fields so nothing has to be retyped. The duplicate branch was kept as-is: 'That reference number is already filed' is more specific than anything generic. Same half-applied-helper shape as the guard-sentence defect - whWriteError existed and this path did not call it. MEASURED AND NOT SWEPT: 115 further sites across 8 pages still pass a raw .message to showToast (project-manager 26, asset-hub 22, logbook 17, marketplace 13, marketplace-seller 13, hive 10, integrations 9, inventory 5). Those are internal CMMS surfaces where a technical string is less harmful and sometimes useful; recorded as a known class rather than claimed as fixed.

evidence.ref: psql: rolled-back txn on service_credit_topups + credit_treasury (2026-08-04)
evidence.asserts: a repeated verify mints once, not twice
evidence.checked: Proven by DOING IT TWICE in a rolled-back transaction and counting the effect, never by reading a guard. (1) SAME GCASH REFERENCE FILED TWICE — the shape a provider produces by double-tapping or re-filing after a timeout whose result they never saw: the second insert raised unique_violation and rows_for_ref stayed 1, so one payment cannot become two claims. (2) THE SAME TOP-UP VERIFIED TWICE — the founder double-clicks the verify control: the first verify minted 500.00 and the second was absorbed as a no-op (the status had already moved, so the mint trigger does not re-fire). TOTAL MINT AFTER TWO VERIFIES = 500.00, not 1000.00, which is the whole question — a double-mint would create credits with no cash behind them and break the cover ratio the treasury exists to guarantee. Rollback verified: topups back to 3, issued back to 1500.00. INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first attempt failed on a NOT NULL payer_auth_uid I had not supplied — my probe, not the product; recorded rather than mistaken for a schema defect.

evidence.checked: Staged a job the completion sweep must act on (completed, window elapsed 10 days) inside a rolled-back txn, ran sweep_service_completions(), and followed the value across the seam. The cron wrote status=settled and the view the UI reads returned settled, with 8 rows visible to that client. All three money crons exist and resolve to real functions (listing-holding-fee-monthly, service-broadcast-sweep-1min, service-completion-sweep-hourly). INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, recorded because it nearly became a false defect: the first run reported "SEAM FAIL: the cron wrote settled and the UI view shows NULL". v_service_request_truth filters on auth.uid(), and a psql session has NO JWT — so the view returned 0 of 12 rows to me regardless of status. Re-ran with set_config(request.jwt.claims) AND role=authenticated for the row's actual client; the seam was intact all along. An RLS-filtered view needs the ROLE and the CLAIMS, not just a query.

FOUND A REAL DEFECT AND FIXED IT, then proved both branches. Nulling the money fields the wallet reads took `available` from PHP-200 to PHP0 -- a fabricated zero, not a stated gap. `Number(row?.available || 0)` turns NULL into 0, and on a balance that is not a rounding detail: PHP0 reads as 'I have nothing' rather than 'we could not read it'. Worse, every branch below keys off `avail < 0`, and null is not less than zero, so a seller who is actually below zero and BLOCKED from publishing would have been shown a calm PHP0 with no explanation and no route.
A SECOND READER had the same bug and would have been missed by fixing only the walked one: the hold preview at :833 also did `Number(row?.available || 0)`, and `bal` drives 'Your credits now', the `after = bal - hold` arithmetic, and _holdState.ok. A null balance would have told the seller they were SHORT, and blocked publishing, on a number nobody read. That panel already had the right concept for a failed read ('unknown rather than zero') -- the null simply never took that path. It does now.
PROVEN BOTH WAYS. With nulls: wallet renders the gap character, the blocked note and the 'Go to top up' route correctly stay hidden, and the hold preview says "can't check right now / Your wallet could not be read, so this figure is unknown rather than zero". With the real network: PHP-200 still renders with note and route shown, and the hold preview still computes -- price PHP5,000.00, held PHP500.00, credits now PHP-200.00, Short by PHP700.00.

evidence.checked:
FOUND AND FIXED ON A FRESH-LOAD RE-CHECK, which is the only reason it was believed. The lens had reported this red mid-sequence and it was deliberately NOT filed, because every red trusted without a clean-load re-check today turned out to be the instrument. Re-run standalone with every money field nulled at the network from first paint, it held.
THE DEFECT: `Number(null)` is 0, so an unreadable top-up amount rendered 'PHP0 · ref 1005556667770' on the queue where an admin matches a filed GCash reference against a real payment BEFORE releasing credits. That is the worst place on this platform for a fabricated zero: it invites either dismissing a real payment as nothing, or releasing credits against a figure the screen never actually had. Two call sites had it -- the pending top-ups queue and the GCash leftovers queue.
It now reads 'amount unreadable' and KEEPS THE REFERENCE VISIBLE, so the admin can go match the payment by hand rather than being left with neither number.
PROVEN BOTH WAYS: nulled, 0 fabricated PHP0, 'amount unreadable' present, ref 1005556667770 still shown, 0 undefined/NaN; healthy, the line reads 'PHP300 · ref 1005556667770' with the real amount intact. This is the same line an earlier session fixed for LAYOUT -- the reference being pushed 41px off screen. That fixed whether an admin could SEE the reference; this fixes whether the amount beside it is true.

findings.title: a hung dependency never resolves into a stated timeout
findings.measured: MEASURED FAILURE, recorded rather than skipped: under a hung dependency this surface does not end in a STATED timeout. Sampled mid-hang with every read held ~9s, the page does not say it timed out, is taking longer, or is slow -- it simply waits. A hang that never resolves into words leaves a visitor unable to tell a slow network from a broken page, and on a public profile the visitor is someone deciding whether to contact this seller at all. The other three failure states on this surface (401, partial, null-field) pass, so this is a specific gap in the timeout path rather than a missing error posture.

evidence.checked:
LANDED ON THE SECOND APPROACH, after the first was vacuous and said so. Re-dispatching DOMContentLoaded touched 0 fields; a category filter chip DID re-query (5 requests) but still touched 0, because my key regex was guessing. Reading the actual response shapes settled it: v_community_posts_truth carries NO numeric fields at all (id, hive_id, author_name, content, category, pinned, flagged, public, timestamps), and community_reactions is (post_id, emoji, worker_name) -- the reaction counts on screen are derived from ROW COUNTS, which a null cannot corrupt. The single nullable numeric this surface reads is v_worker_achievements_truth.current_level.
Targeting that one: 22 levels nulled via the filter-chip re-query, and the surface behaved. No fabricated 'Level 0' appeared, no undefined or NaN reached the text, and the tier badges were unchanged at 3 before and after -- correctly, since they come from trust_tier rather than from the level.
THE SUBJECT IS NARROW AND THAT IS THE FINDING AS MUCH AS THE PASS: on a surface whose data is almost entirely text and derived counts, this oracle has exactly one field to bite on. Saying so is worth more than a green that implies the whole page was exercised. | RE-WALKED 2026-08-04 on community.html after the error-taxonomy fix (failures(): no fabricated zero, no undefined/NaN).

evidence.checked:
0 raw enums reaching a person, scanned across 5 states: the Parts / Training / Hiring / Services section tabs and the listing DETAIL SHEET, where a listing's own status is most likely to leak. findings.title: offline write fires instead of being refused; the widget promised it was queued
findings.measured:
WALKED LIVE 2026-08-04 and the surface does NOT refuse before firing. Offline (navigator.onLine forced false + the offline event the platform's own banner listens for), the seller's Save issued TWO writes -- POST marketplace_sellers?on_conflict=worker_name and POST hive_audit_log. They were intercepted by the probe and never forwarded, so nothing was written, but they LEFT the page: there is no pre-flight guard.
AND THE PLATFORM WAS TELLING THE READER THE OPPOSITE. The shared connectivity widget promised, on every page, that 'Pending writes save to this device and drain automatically when the connection returns. You can keep working offline.' That is true on the six pages that register a queue (asset-hub, community, dayplanner, inventory, logbook, project-manager). It was false on all four marketplace surfaces, which register NO queue -- and three of them LOAD offline-queue.js without ever calling it. whGetQueueDepth() returns {total:0, perSurface:{}} on the seller. So on exactly the screens where money moves, a provider was told their work was safe while an offline Save fired into a dead network and was lost.
FIXED, the honest half: the widget now computes its own sentence from whether THIS page registered a queue, and says 'This page does not save work offline. Anything you submit without a connection will not be sent, so wait until you are back online.' Proven both ways -- the seller (perSurface {}) shows the warning, community (perSurface {community:0}) still shows the original promise, so the fix did not simply swap one false sentence for another.
STILL OPEN, and the reason this row is owed rather than green: the BEHAVIOUR is unchanged. The write still fires offline and is still lost; only the copy is now truthful. Closing this row means either a pre-flight refusal on the marketplace writes or real queue adoption on those four surfaces -- the per-page queue integration that PHASE 2 already recorded as a deferred follow-on. Queueing a GCash top-up FILING offline is not a trivial call either: a filing that drains later can arrive after the provider has given up and re-filed, which is the duplicate the unique index exists to refuse.

findings.title: offline write fires instead of being refused; the widget promised it was queued
findings.measured:
WALKED LIVE 2026-08-04 and the surface does NOT refuse before firing. Offline (navigator.onLine forced false + the offline event the platform's own banner listens for), the seller's Save issued TWO writes -- POST marketplace_sellers?on_conflict=worker_name and POST hive_audit_log. They were intercepted by the probe and never forwarded, so nothing was written, but they LEFT the page: there is no pre-flight guard.
AND THE PLATFORM WAS TELLING THE READER THE OPPOSITE. The shared connectivity widget promised, on every page, that 'Pending writes save to this device and drain automatically when the connection returns. You can keep working offline.' That is true on the six pages that register a queue (asset-hub, community, dayplanner, inventory, logbook, project-manager). It was false on all four marketplace surfaces, which register NO queue -- and three of them LOAD offline-queue.js without ever calling it. whGetQueueDepth() returns {total:0, perSurface:{}} on the seller. So on exactly the screens where money moves, a provider was told their work was safe while an offline Save fired into a dead network and was lost.
FIXED, the honest half: the widget now computes its own sentence from whether THIS page registered a queue, and says 'This page does not save work offline. Anything you submit without a connection will not be sent, so wait until you are back online.' Proven both ways -- the seller (perSurface {}) shows the warning, community (perSurface {community:0}) still shows the original promise, so the fix did not simply swap one false sentence for another.
STILL OPEN, and the reason this row is owed rather than green: the BEHAVIOUR is unchanged. The write still fires offline and is still lost; only the copy is now truthful. Closing this row means either a pre-flight refusal on the marketplace writes or real queue adoption on those four surfaces -- the per-page queue integration that PHASE 2 already recorded as a deferred follow-on. Queueing a GCash top-up FILING offline is not a trivial call either: a filing that drains later can arrive after the provider has given up and re-filed, which is the duplicate the unique index exists to refuse.

scenarios.oracle: text meets WCAG AA 4.5:1 against its ACTUAL composited background, alpha included - the trap that made every tinted pill read 1.00

findings.title: axe reported 0 violations and 185 INCOMPLETE; a scan that abstains is not a pass
findings.measured:
MY OWN FALSE GREEN, CAUGHT AND WITHDRAWN. This row was banked green on 'axe ran with 0 violations at every state'. axe reported 0 VIOLATIONS and 185 INCOMPLETE nodes on this surface -- 158 of them for the single reason "Element's background color could not be determined due to a background gradient", plus 9 obscured, 11 non-text, 7 too-short. axe does not fail those; it ABSTAINS on them, and a scan that abstains on 185 nodes has not established that the text on this page meets WCAG AA. It established that it could not tell. The platform has recorded this exact class before (axe '0 violations' = FALSE 100, 233 SERIOUS incomplete), and I walked into it anyway by reading the violations count and not the incomplete count.
The same blindness sits on every gradient-backed surface: marketplace 185 incomplete, marketplace-seller 39.
WHAT CAN MEASURE THEM: the BH APCA lens, because its compositor averages gradient colour stops instead of giving up -- the same fix that stopped it scoring the seller's Save button as 'invisible'. So on precisely the nodes where axe abstains, APCA has a number, and that number says 273 of 552 text nodes across the seven surfaces are below their perceptual floor. contrast_wcag is OWED until the WCAG question is answered for the abstained nodes rather than assumed from a violations count of zero.

scenarios.question: contrast, focus, motion and naming - the things a screenshot cannot confirm and a measurement can
scenarios.oracle: the same text passes the APCA perceptual threshold for its size and weight

findings.title: APCA: 103 of 126 text nodes sit below their perceptual floor while WCAG AA passes
findings.measured: Measured live 2026-08-04 with a gradient-aware compositor. The instrument was verified against APCA's published anchors BEFORE any verdict was recorded: black on white 106.0, white on black -107.9, #888 on white 63.1 -- all matching. It was also wrong once and corrected: reading backgroundColor alone reported the seller's Save button as Lc 0 ('invisible') when it is dark navy on a BRIGHT ORANGE gradient, and 41 of 49 text nodes on that surface sit over a gradient, so nearly every first reading was false. Averaging the gradient's colour stops fixed it and the Save button left the failure list. Worst on this surface: 10-11px category and trust chips at Lc 45-58. axe-core reports 0 WCAG violations on the same text, which is the point: WCAG grades a contrast RATIO and APCA grades perceptual lightness, and they disagree hardest on small text. NOT FIXED: the cause is the platform's small-text colour tokens at 10-13px, so the remedy changes how the product LOOKS across every surface. That is Ian's call, not a probe's.

findings.title: a REJECTED top-up could be revived and minted in two statements by any platform admin
findings.measured: The mint fires only on pending_verification -> verified, so a direct rejected -> verified flip is inert and the ledger does not move -- which is exactly what made this look safe. Nothing constrained the transition itself. Probed as a real platform admin (role authenticated, JWT sub = the admin's uid; a postgres superuser probe would have proven nothing about a guard that reads auth.uid()): STEP1 rejected->pending SUCCEEDED, STEP2 pending->verified SUCCEEDED, ledger 3 -> 4, 'MINTED FROM A REJECTED TOP-UP: topup 777.00'.
findings.why_it_matters: Every credit in this economy originates at this one table, and rejection is the only thing standing between a GCash payment that never arrived and spendable money. A rejection that the person who issued it can walk back is not a decision, it is a suggestion.
findings.fix: mig 20260803000040 freezes both terminal states: once verified or rejected, a top-up's status cannot change for anyone acting as a person. Legal transitions remain exactly pending_verification -> verified (mints once) and pending_verification -> rejected (mints nothing). The no-JWT backend path and the announced workhive.service_system_write bypass stay exempt so seeders and sweeps keep working, matching the sibling intake-immutability guard.
findings.teeth: T1 revive rejected->pending REFUSED 23514; T2 direct rejected->verified REFUSED 23514; T3 pending->verified still mints (1 ledger row); T4 pending->rejected still works; mig 38 auto-match still reaches topup=verified/receipt=matched and mints 1; no-JWT seeder rewrite of a decided row still OK.

scenarios.oracle: buyer -X and provider +X, circulation delta EXACTLY 0, and no reward is also earned on that job -- earn or spend, never both

findings.title: three more readers still split one person's wallet in two -- and it made EVERY credit payment impossible
findings.measured: mig 39 unified the wallet for three readers and missed three: guard_reward_spend_cap (the balance check behind every credit payment), my_credit_balance() (what the buyer's own confirm sheet reads), and apply_dispute_adjustment (the bound on what an adjudication recovers). Measured live: every credit in this economy sits in the PROVIDER namespace -- three provider accounts hold it, there is not one consumer row. On an 800 job (10% cap 80) with the person holding 340: 'the guard SEES 0' and spending 80 was REFUSED 23514 'Not enough credits: balance is PHP0, this would spend PHP80.'
findings.why_it_matters: This is not an edge case, it is the whole feature. With all credits provider-side, NO buyer could spend credits at all -- the spend half of the earn-or-spend switch had never been able to fire. And the refusal takes the cruellest shape a money error can: it tells someone holding PHP340 that their balance is zero. my_credit_balance() is the same bug one layer up, so the sheet offered no spend field and the buyer never even reached the refusal -- screen and guard agreed, and both were wrong. apply_dispute_adjustment is quieter but costs real money: it under-reads what a provider still holds, so the difference is silently booked as a shortfall the PLATFORM absorbs while the provider keeps credits the adjudication said to return.
findings.fix: mig 20260803000041 repoints all three at person_credit_balance(). No ledger row moves -- the ledger is append-only and its history is correct; only the readers change, exactly as mig 39 did. A namespace may go negative while the PERSON stays positive: a namespace is a bookkeeping location, not a wallet.
findings.teeth: A: the refused spend now ACCEPTED, person 340 -> 260. B: one peso over the 10% cap still REFUSED 23514. C: a person holding 0 across BOTH namespaces still REFUSED 23514. my_credit_balance() as the signed-in buyer returns 340.00 (was 0). All four credit gates green: solvency, loop-closes, guards-refuse, posture.

findings.title: all four halves of the spend oracle hold, end to end through apply_credits_to_request
findings.measured: BEFORE buyer=340 provider=1000 circulation=1140 -> apply_credits_to_request(job, 80) -> AFTER buyer=260 provider=1080 circulation=1140. Legs: reward_spend -80 (buyer) and reward_fund +80 (provider), both consumer-namespace, so circulation delta is EXACTLY 0 -- a transfer, never a mint. Fourth half: inserting a reward_earn on that same job was REFUSED 23514 by guard_reward_exclusive. Earn or spend, never both.

findings.title: the 10,000,000 supply cap did not watch the only door credits actually use
findings.measured: issue_credits() is the ceiling -- it takes authorised - issued FOR UPDATE, refuses when the remainder is too small, and increments issued_credits. Exactly ONE function called it: claim_starter_grant. The other mint, in guard_service_topup_status on every verified GCash top-up, inserted its ledger row directly and never touched the treasury. Live: credit_treasury issued = 0.00 while the ledger held topup = 1,500.00 across 2 rows (starter_grant = 0 rows). Every credit that exists came through the door nobody was counting.
findings.why_it_matters: Two consequences. (1) The cap was UNENFORCED on the primary mint path: issued_credits never grew, so authorised - issued was always the full 10,000,000 and no top-up could ever be refused for exhausting supply -- the ceiling that 'guarantees every credit in circulation is honourable' guarded a door credits do not use. (2) The founder console reads authorised_credits and issued_credits from v_credit_posture to state the platform's own position, and showed 0 issued while PHP1,500 circulated. A money figure that is confidently wrong is worse than one that is missing.
findings.fix: mig 20260803000042: the top-up mint now issues against the ceiling, exactly as the starter grant does, BEFORE the ledger insert -- so a refusal aborts the statement and the refusal and the mint can never disagree. issued_credits back-filled from the ledger (0.00 -> 1,500.00); a counter corrected to match the rows it summarises is not a history rewrite, and the append-only ledger was untouched. The migration RAISES if the two still disagree afterwards.
findings.teeth: A: verifying a PHP500 top-up with only PHP100 unissued was REFUSED 23514, 0 ledger rows written, and the status stayed pending_verification so the founder can retry after a governance decision. B: a PHP100 top-up against exactly PHP100 remaining MINTED and drove remaining to 0.00. Screen half, walked live in platform-actions: the toast read the guard's own sentence verbatim -- 'Only 100 credits remain unissued; cannot issue 500. The supply is capped at 10,000,000 and that ceiling is what guarantees every credit in circulation is honourable.' -- not the generic 'Action failed. Try again.' All four credit gates green afterwards.

findings.title: an objection inside the window reaches disputed, and the sweep provably steps over it
findings.measured: Two jobs staged completed 10 days ago, both past the 3-day objection deadline. The buyer objected to one: raise_service_objection returned {ok:true}, the job moved completed -> disputed, and the reason was journalled to service_job_events ('buyer raised a problem inside the objection window: The unit still leaks after the visit'). Then the sweep ran ONCE over both: {settled: 1, unpriced: 0} -- the objected job stayed disputed and the CONTROL settled, which is the non-vacuity proof that the sweep really executed rather than silently matching nothing. The control's payment carries auto_confirmed_at set and confirmed_by NULL, so an auto-settlement is never recorded as a person attesting to the amount. A second sweep in the same transaction returned {settled: 0} -- idempotent.
findings.note: raise_service_objection also refuses a non-client caller ('Only the person who hailed this job can raise a problem with it'), a job that is not yet completed, and an empty reason. Observation, not a defect: every transition writes a note-less row via trg_journal_service_request (21 of 22 live events have a blank note) and the objection adds a second, enriched row -- so a disputed job shows two journal rows. Nothing renders service_job_events, so this is internal-only.

findings.title: tools/probe_adversarial_personas.py -- the four personas walked as PEOPLE, each asserting containment AND a readable refusal
findings.measured: All four contained, every refusal legible, exit 0, ledger byte-identical before and after (5 rows / PHP1,140) with zero residue. spammer: capped at 3 live listings -- 'A new seller can keep 3 listings live until one of them sells. You have 3 - sell one, or take one down to make room. This is not about the credits.' sybil: second claim returns {"reason": "already_claimed", "granted": false}. collusive pair: a naked user-to-user transfer REFUSED with 'Credits cannot be moved between people. They are earned on a purchase and spent on a purchase' and circulation delta exactly 0.00. scam provider: the buyer gets a dated deadline (2026-08-06) and raise_service_objection returns {ok:true}, moving the job to disputed.
findings.why_it_matters: The 500-run simulation proved the ECONOMICS hold. It never proved the SCREEN refuses these people in words they can act on -- and a guard that blocks in silence cannot be told apart from a guard that is not firing at all. So each persona asserts two things, and a bare 'violates check constraint' fails the readability bar.
findings.note: THE PROBE'S OWN THREE BUGS ARE WHY IT IS TRUSTWORTHY, and each is a banked class. (1) It read only stdout while every verdict line is a psql NOTICE on stderr -- all four reported 'no verdict line', a false red. (2) It probed the spam cap with NO JWT, and guard_first_listings_need_a_sale opens with `if auth.uid() is null return new` (the backend path seeders need), so all 8 listings published and it read as 'the cap does not work' when the probe was never a person -- the 'an RLS probe needs the ROLE, not just claims' lesson, applied to a trigger. (3) Even with an identity, TWO earlier guards fired first: self-publish is refused outright, then the reservation guard refused for want of credits -- so the cap was never consulted and a PASS proved only the outermost gate, the 'survivor masked by a sibling constraint' shape. It now funds the seller and selects one already AT the cap by the cap's own arithmetic, so the deepest layer is the one that answers. Registered in run_platform_checks as gate `adversarial-personas`.
